model.architecture: `Olmo2ForCausalLM` rides the stock converter with no custom code: QK-norm and OLMo-2's reordered post-norm lower to generic ops.

variants.quantization: int4 weights — blockwise (block 32) + OCTAV optimal-clipping, symmetric; embedding int8

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 23.08 tok/s decode / 548.2 prefill, peak 931 MB, init 5.0 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-24, 1 run) against CPU 11.52-12.1 decode / 96.0-168.7 prefill, peak 2147 MB, init 1.4 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken - a measured win for gpu on decode (2.0x) and prefill

platform_notes: iPhone prefill figure was measured on a short chat prompt and is dominated by fixed per-turn overhead; not comparable to the 256-token desktop prefill column.
At 0.93 GB it fits comfortably on an 8 GB phone (Android).
Whole bundle is a single sub-2 GiB section, so it memory-maps on iOS without an externalized embedder.
Fits and runs on a Pixel 8a (8 GB) via Gallery; no timing was taken there (backend not stated).
The same bundle runs on macOS, Linux and Windows (desktop CLI).
Mac CPU benchmark figures are noisy: six invocations spread CPU decode over 29.0–33.3 tok/s, so treat the CPU row as ±7%.
Not a measured row: card reports iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 27.0) gpu prefill_tps 27.6, decode_tps 24.4, ttft_s 0.95 (Performance — iPhone 17 Pro on-device table; runtime/run count not stated)

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (1375 ops across 2 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: Files downloaded before 2026-08-30 carry the GPT-2 default pre-tokenizer instead of the model's own regex (digit groups and punctuation-before-newline split differently; role markers differed by 3 tokens per turn). Re-download.
Accuracy figures and on-device (iPhone) rows were measured on the previous (pre-2026-08-30) file; the on-device gate has not been re-run on the current file.
Prompts containing accented letters, symbols or emoji now tokenize differently from the previous file, so individual answers to such prompts can change.
int4 costs about 9 GSM8K points against bf16 at this size (63.0% vs 72.0%, n=100).
